Question: As Emily is riding her bicycle on a long straight road, she spots Emerson skating in the same direction \(\frac{1}{2}\) mile in front of her. After she passes him, she can see him in her rear view mirror until he is \(\frac{1}{2}\) mile behind her. Emily rides at a constant rate of \(12\) miles per hour, and Emerson skates at a constant rate of \(8\) miles per hour. For how many minutes can Emily see Emerson?
Solution:
Emily first sees Emerson \(\frac12\) mile ahead and last sees him \(\frac12\) mile behind. During that interval, she gains a total of
\[
\frac12+\frac12=1\text{ mile}
\]
on him.

Because they travel in the same direction, Emily gains distance at \(12-8=4\) miles per hour. The time needed to gain \(1\) mile is therefore
\[
1\div4=\frac14\text{ hour}.
\]
Since an hour contains \(60\) minutes, she can see Emerson for \(\frac14\cdot60=\boxed{15}\) minutes, choice D.
